title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Tunnel Ping Pong Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, RFC 9220 parser regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler reads a masked client ping frame through `Http3WebSocketTunnelContext`, writes an unmasked pong frame with the same payload, and then continues using the same tunnel for a text message and response.
preconditions: The WebSocket frame parser remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
The accepted tunnel message helper boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0004`.
expected_result: The focused loopback and parser tests pass, the new RFC 9220 ping/pong requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server handler path now has locally verified WebSocket ping-to-pong behavior on accepted RFC 9220 tunnels while preserving the same stream for later data. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
